title: CastillosCVEP40
description: A code-modulated Visual Evoked Potential (c-VEP) derivative dataset from 12 healthy participants, specifically focusing on the 40% amplitude depth modulation m-sequence c-VEP condition. This dataset is derived from a study comparing burst and m-sequence stimulus patterns at two amplitude levels (100% and 40% depth modulation) for reactive brain-computer interface applications. The study evaluated classification performance using convolutional neural networks, demonstrating that the reduced amplitude condition (40%) maintained 94.2% accuracy while improving visual comfort compared to the full amplitude burst c-VEP condition which achieved 95.6% accuracy.
methods_description: EEG data acquired from 12 healthy participants using a BrainProducts LiveAmp system (32 channels, 500 Hz sampling rate, FCz reference). Factorial experimental design with four conditions: burst vs m-sequence patterns × 100% vs 40% amplitude depth modulation. Each trial consisted of a 0.5s visual cue (red-bordered square) followed by 2.2s stimulation phase and 0.7s inter-trial interval. Stimuli presented on a 60 Hz Dell monitor with four target locations (150 pixels each). Preprocessing included average re-referencing, IIR notch filtering (49.9-50.1 Hz, order 16), and baseline removal. Classification performed using convolutional neural networks with sliding window feature extraction for bitwise decoding.
